newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes find support, major dominates Oman.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes find support, major dominates Oman.

text.p: Crude prices in Asia rebounded slightly on Friday following the downward correction through the middle part of the week.
But traders said players moved to the sidelines of the futures markets to wait for clearer short term direction.
By late afternoon on Friday, the December Brent contract was up 24 cents at $23.99 in London. NYMEX had firmed overnight on the after-hours ACCESS system in a modest rebound.
Traders said the paper market in Asia was mostly quiet on Friday with Brent/Dubai mostly steady although December came in slightly on the weaker Brent overnight.
Dubai intermonth spreads were also steady.

Several paper Tapis deals for November were concluded on Thursday at $24.55, $24.60 (x2) and $24.65. January was traded at $24.00 and the first quarter traded twice at $23.50 and $23.60. A second-quarter deal was also done at $21.77, market sources said.
The wet market was mostly focused on Oman, with another trade emerging at MPM plus 10 cents, this time with a European major selling into China.
Traders said a major had acquired several cargos of December Oman in trading this month, when usually it is a seller.
Traders estimated that with the exception of the major, availabilities of Oman for December were another major with one cargo, China possibly with one cargo and a trader with a small parcel.
A Japanese trader, who had two cargos available, was awarded the Bangchak tender, traders and industry sources said, taking those availabilities off the shelf.
Traders said some Lower Zakum cargoes were still available.
